topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, lecture scope, and learning objectives for understanding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology, Genetic Predisposition, and Environmental Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises through genetic and evolutionary processes, weighing endogenous stochastic factors against environmental exposures and geographic epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious microorganisms drive malignant transformation, using the mechanistic link between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Direct and Metabolically Activated Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which environmental, dietary, and chemical mutagens undergo xenobiotic processing and directly damage cellular DNA.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic drivers of oncogenesis, focusing on inflammatory microenvironments, multistage promoter activity, and developmental windows of tissue vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the experimental, genomic, toxicological, and epidemiological strategies used to assess mutagenic activity and determine carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer delivers closing remarks summarizing environmental cancer risks and contextualizing daily exposure decisions within a risk-benefit framework.
